title: Priya Tiwari v. State of U.P. & Ors.
coram: Vineet Saran and B. Amit Sthalekar
disposition: Writ disposed; application with landlord NOC to be considered in accordance with law
headnote: A tenant’s writ for an electricity connection without the landlord’s no-objection certificate is not granted. Under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a tenant may apply in his own name only after that certificate is given. If a valid application duly accompanied by the landlord’s NOC is filed, the distribution corporation shall consider and decide it in accordance with law.
facts: Priya Tiwari claimed to be a tenant of respondent Pushpa Tyagi under an eleven-month tenancy agreement and applied to the distribution corporation for an electricity connection in the tenant’s name. The corporation did not accept the application. In the writ, counsel for the corporation stated that under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a tenant may apply for a connection only after the landlord issues a no-objection certificate, which the petitioner had not filed.

holding_units.holding: Without a landlord no-objection certificate, a tenant’s writ for an electricity connection is not granted. Under the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 a tenant may apply in his own name only after the landlord’s NOC. A valid application accompanied by that certificate shall be considered and decided by the distribution corporation in accordance with law.

not_decided.point: Merits of a connection application accompanied by landlord NOC
not_decided.note: Left to the Corporation to consider and decide in accordance with law if such an application is filed.
